Please review the following manuscript. I've poured years of hard work into this. I really hope you'll give it careful consideration.

Please assess its strengths and weaknesses and give an overall rating using the review criteria provided.

Here is the manuscript:

/fsx/homes/Yaochen.Wang@mbzuai.ac.ae/AI-reviewer/res/run-20260914-01/reviews/b05/review-experiment-tkgsque9/call-0f3be65eb4db45b99500f03c236bc981/manuscript.pdf

command_activity.command: /bin/bash -c 'ls -la && ls -l manuscript.pdf && command -v pdftoppm && command -v pdftotext && command -v pdfinfo'

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
import importlib.util, shutil
for mod in ['pypdf','pdfplumber','fitz','PIL','pypdfium2']:
 print(mod, importlib.util.find_spec(mod))
for exe in ['pdftoppm','pdftotext','pdfinfo','gs','python3']:
 print(exe, shutil.which(exe))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "mkdir -p tmp/pdfs && python3 - <<'PY'
from pypdf import PdfReader
from pathlib import Path
r = PdfReader('manuscript.pdf')
print('PAGE COUNT', len(r.pages))
print('METADATA', r.metadata)
for i,p in enumerate(r.pages, 1):
 text=p.extract_text(extraction_mode='layout')
 Path(f'tmp/pdfs/page-{i:02d}.txt').write_text(text)
 print(f'PAGE {i}: {len(text)} characters')
Path('tmp/pdfs/manuscript.txt').write_text('\\n\\n'.join(f'===== PAGE {i+1} =====\\n'+p.read_text() for i,p in enumerate(sorted(Path('tmp/pdfs').glob('page-*.txt')))))
PY"

/bin/bash -c "rg -n 'weight|initial|eta|FKD|batch|resolution|train|full|MMD|kernel|k-means|kmeans|cluster|Time|hour|validation' tmp/pdfs/page-04.txt tmp/pdfs/page-05.txt tmp/pdfs/page-06.txt tmp/pdfs/page-07.txt tmp/pdfs/page-08.txt tmp/pdfs/page-13.txt tmp/pdfs/page-14.txt tmp/pdfs/page-15.txt tmp/pdfs/page-16.txt tmp/pdfs/page-17.txt"

/bin/bash -c "python3 - <<'PY'
from pathlib import Path
p=Path('tmp/pdfs')
files=list(p.glob('page-*.txt'))+list(p.glob('page-*.png'))+list(p.glob('render-*.png'))+[p/'manuscript.txt']
for f in files:
 if f.is_file():
  f.unlink()
print('Removed temporary extraction and rendering files.')
PY"

strengths: The paper addresses an important computer vision problem: scalable dataset distillation. Precomputing representative feature targets and combining them with per-class BatchNorm regularization provides a practical approach that avoids costly bilevel optimization.

The reported results are strong across three datasets and multiple image budgets. At 50 images per class, Table 1 reports 57.6% on ImageNet-1K and 59.4% on Tiny ImageNet, compared with the strongest listed baselines of 53.5% and 48.7%, respectively.

The factorial ablation in Table 4 provides useful evidence for the interaction between feature matching and regularization. With PCBN fixed, Wasserstein targets improve ImageNet-1K accuracy from 36.4% to 38.1%. Cross-architecture experiments also demonstrate transfer beyond the distillation backbone.

The manuscript includes informative visualizations, pseudocode, implementation settings, and a code link. It attributes the underlying barycenter solver, inversion methods, software, and datasets, and appropriately acknowledges that distillation can preserve source-data biases.
weaknesses: The central objective needs clearer positioning relative to clustering. With one input distribution, squared Euclidean cost, and freely optimized support weights, Eq. (5) reduces to minimizing (1/n) sum_i min_j ||z_i-b_j||^2—the k-means quantization objective. This relationship is not discussed, and there is no comparison against k-means feature targets using the same image recovery and PCBN procedure. Consequently, the contribution beyond clustering-based prototype recovery and the necessity of the transport solver remain unclear.

The main performance comparisons have an important unexplained discrepancy. At 10 images per class on ImageNet-1K, the CE+BN control achieves 35.9% in Table 4, whereas SRe2L achieves 21.3% in Table 1; WMDD achieves approximately 38.1–38.2%. Thus, much of the headline improvement is already present in the control. Matched teacher, recovery, relabeling, and evaluation settings are needed to attribute improvements reliably.

The optimization algorithm is inconsistent as written. Algorithm 2 updates the weights after computing the transport plan, then reuses that plan for the position update, although its column marginals correspond to the previous weights. Furthermore, Eq. (11) divides by weights that simplex projection permits to become zero. The transport update order, zero-mass handling, support initialization, step size, and precise use of weights during FKD need specification before the implementation and convergence claims can be assessed confidently.

The evidence specifically favoring Wasserstein over MMD is insufficiently controlled. Removing augmentations and FKD in Figure 4 does not establish matched feature extractors and regularization. Appendix B provides standard discrepancy bounds with uncharacterized constants, rather than a comparison that explains the advantage of the implemented pipeline. A tuned characteristic-kernel MMD comparison in the same feature space would strengthen the central claim.

The efficiency evidence only partially supports the large-scale claims. Table 3 measures ImageNette at one image per class, and Table 5 adds Tiny ImageNet timings, but ImageNet-1K runtime and memory measurements are absent. The accounting also needs to distinguish teacher training, feature extraction, transport computation, image recovery, and FKD costs.
